attention.dense_execution.boundary: Own the attention result for a specified mask, head layout and sequence position. A failing attention row can be reproduced with fixed Q, K and V independently of the cache allocator.
attention.dense_execution.summary: Compare each query with the keys it is allowed to see and use the resulting weights to combine their values.

backend.execute_operators.boundary: Own shape and dtype admission, fallback and launch. The same correct model operator can dispatch to an incompatible device kernel.
backend.execute_operators.summary: Choose and run a CPU or GPU kernel that supports the operation’s tensor shapes and data types.

batch.execution_layout.boundary: Turn admitted requests into offsets, positions and state handles. A batch can be scheduled fairly yet still mix two sequences’ rows.
batch.execution_layout.summary: Map each scheduled token to a batch row, its sequence position and the state it reads or updates.

decode.advance_sequence.boundary: Own the transition from committed token and sequence state to next-step logits. Cached execution can be compared with full-context recomputation.
decode.advance_sequence.summary: Run a prompt or the next token through the model, update the sequence state and return scores for the following token.

dense.feed_forward.boundary: Where the layer configuration selects a dense FFN, verify its projections, activation and residual shape without expert selection or token packing.
dense.feed_forward.summary: Transform each token’s hidden vector using the dense layer’s projections and activation function.

engine.expert_streaming.boundary: Own a demanded weight range from admission through read completion and last use. One controller must protect slots and enforce the byte ceiling.
engine.expert_streaming.summary: Load the selected experts into available memory slots and keep their weights there until the calculation finishes.

graph.lower_capture_replay.boundary: A captured graph is a reusable executable with validity constraints. Qualify pointer, shape and state changes against uncaptured execution before enabling replay.
graph.lower_capture_replay.summary: Turn model operations into device work and replay repeated launches when their shapes and buffers are compatible.

memory.reusable_sessions.boundary: Share cached prefixes only across compatible identities. A correct per-sequence KV allocator can still reuse stale prefix content across requests.
memory.reusable_sessions.summary: Find stored state for a matching prompt prefix so the engine can resume from it and skip repeated work.

memory.runtime_arenas.boundary: Own physical workspace lifetimes and alignment across operators. Verify peak live bytes and overlap separately from model arithmetic.
memory.runtime_arenas.summary: Reserve memory for working buffers and let operations reuse a buffer once its last reader finishes.

memory.sequence_kv.boundary: Own the mapping from logical position to live KV bytes, including migration and reclamation. Moving a page must update the same map that readers use.
memory.sequence_kv.summary: Map each token position to the memory holding its attention keys and values so later tokens can read them.

merge.expert_contributions.boundary: Own both ends of token permutation. Packing and weighted reconstruction must agree on token identity, order and aligned mixture weights.
merge.expert_contributions.summary: Group token rows by expert, then return each result to its original token and add it with the correct weight.

model.decoder_architecture.boundary: Own block order, residual state and site-specific normalization. A passing kernel can still be inserted at the wrong residual boundary.
model.decoder_architecture.summary: Connect attention, feed-forward layers, normalization and residual additions in the order the checkpoint specifies.

model.embedding_service.boundary: Map vocabulary IDs to the exact checkpoint rows and embedding representation consumed by the first layer. Verify with known IDs before testing the stack.
model.embedding_service.summary: Look up each token ID in the model’s embedding table to get the vector that enters the first layer.

model.expert_routing.boundary: Produce authoritative expert IDs and corresponding unbiased mixture weights. This decision can be checked before loading or executing an expert.
model.expert_routing.summary: Choose which experts run for each token and give each selected expert a weight for combining its answer.

model.logit_head.boundary: Turn the final hidden row into vocabulary logits under the checkpoint’s projection and output transform. This is a small independently testable boundary between model math and sampling.
model.logit_head.summary: Turn the final hidden vector into one score for each possible next token.

observability.runtime_events.boundary: Own optional source annotations, correlation IDs and their measured overhead. Kernel owners expose hooks; the lab interprets the resulting trace.
observability.runtime_events.summary: Add timing and tracing hooks so a profiler can tell which request, layer or expert was running or waiting.

placement.partition_model.boundary: Produce a feasible placement plan for the target and the deployed pack. The runtime cache then enforces that plan under real demand.
placement.partition_model.summary: Decide which weights stay in memory and which must be read from storage, leaving room for the running requests.

routing.forecast_expert_demand.boundary: A predictor emits optional time-bounded hints. Held-out demand can score its lead time and wasted bytes independently of routing correctness.
routing.forecast_expert_demand.summary: Predict which experts to fetch early so their weights can be ready when the router makes its actual selection.

sampling.select_tokens.boundary: Convert logits into a selected token under an explicit sampling policy, seed and constraints. Replay with frozen logits.
sampling.select_tokens.summary: Choose the next token from the vocabulary scores using the request’s rules and sampling settings.

scheduler.request_lifecycle.boundary: Own admission, fairness and slot retirement under capacity constraints. The batch layout worker consumes the accepted assignments.
scheduler.request_lifecycle.summary: Choose which requests run next, reserve their resources and release their slots when they finish or are cancelled.

serving.request_gateway.boundary: Own the interface a client, launcher or profiler uses from outside the engine image. The builder packages it, runtime observability produces the events, and the lab exercises the published interface.
serving.request_gateway.summary: Define how clients send requests and receive results, how the launcher mounts files and how operators access diagnostics.

tokenizer.prepare_request.boundary: Own text-to-ID and committed-ID-to-text conventions, including incremental buffering. Both ends depend on the same vocabulary and special-token rules.
tokenizer.prepare_request.summary: Turn a formatted text prompt into the model’s token IDs and turn committed output IDs back into text.

weights.decode_blocks.boundary: Own the runtime interpretation of bytes, block metadata and scales. A format-specific fixture can fail even when the manifest and exporter pass.
weights.decode_blocks.summary: Decode packed weights into numbers or rearrange their blocks into the layout a kernel needs.

weights.load_checkpoint.boundary: Admit a complete tensor inventory and bind names and offsets to the model. Reject incompatible packs before any kernel consumes them.
weights.load_checkpoint.summary: Find each weight tensor in the checkpoint files and verify its shape, format and byte range before the engine uses it.

weights.prepare_artifact.boundary: Produce a reproducible deployable pack and record how it was made. A new conversion can be evaluated independently with the same runtime decoder.
weights.prepare_artifact.summary: Convert the model’s weights into files the engine can read, using the layout and precision chosen for the build.

model.expert_ffn.boundary: Consume ready expert weights and assigned rows and return per-expert activations. A fixed expert fixture isolates projection errors from routing or cache policy.
model.expert_ffn.summary: Run each selected expert’s feed-forward calculation on the token rows assigned to it.

compiler.engine_contract.boundary: Turn the reviewed intent brief and system ontology into a versioned contract with model obligations, budgets and measurable acceptance gates.
compiler.engine_contract.summary: Turn the reviewed request and system ontology into engine requirements, resource limits and measurable acceptance criteria.

factory.workflow_planning.boundary: Bind each deliverable to a work order, dependencies and an acceptance decision. Several agents may share the same CC.
factory.workflow_planning.summary: Inspect what already works and use the available evidence to choose the next job and assign its CCs to an agent.

factory.source_integration.boundary: Produce a reviewable diff from the work order, including any optional annotation changes, before the independent build.
factory.source_integration.summary: Make the assigned change in the source tree and give the builder a tested, reviewable patch.

factory.builder.boundary: Turn the revision and diff into an identified executable image. Its manifest makes it possible to reproduce the candidate that was measured.
factory.builder.summary: Build a runnable image from the identified source revision and record the dependencies needed to reproduce it.

factory.controlled_experiment.boundary: Own controls, measurement and verdict together. Quantization quality, latency and storage measurements must refer to the same candidate and trial.
factory.controlled_experiment.summary: Run the identified engine image on a fixed workload and use the measurements to decide which contract requirements it meets.

parallel.expert_exchange.boundary: Extension for distributed expert dispatch and the return mapping of remote outputs.
parallel.expert_exchange.summary: Send token rows to the devices holding their selected experts and return the results to the devices that own the tokens.

parallel.model_execution.boundary: Extension for rank-local work, collectives and transfer of prefill state between workers.
parallel.model_execution.summary: Split model computation across devices and pass intermediate results between them.

sequence.recurrent_execution.boundary: Extension for models whose next step consumes a recurrent state rather than only the attention cache.
sequence.recurrent_execution.summary: Update each sequence’s recurrent state after a token and carry that state into the next step.

decode.speculative_execution.boundary: Extension for a proposer, target verification and rollback of rejected state.
decode.speculative_execution.summary: Propose several tokens at once, check them with the target model and undo state changes for rejected tokens.

attention.sparse_execution.boundary: Extension for selecting candidate blocks before attention over a subset of KV.
attention.sparse_execution.summary: Find the positions allowed by the model’s sparse attention rule and compute attention over those keys and values.

weights.adapter_binding.boundary: Extension for composing adapter parameters with a base revision and isolating their effects.
weights.adapter_binding.summary: Load the requested adapter and apply its changes to the matching model projections for that request.

compiler.intent_brief.boundary: Capture the user’s goals, constraints, preferences and open decisions in a reviewed intent brief. Preserve their provenance for the Contract Compiler.
compiler.intent_brief.summary: Record what the user wants to build, which constraints are fixed and which questions still need answers.
